sanskrit: sa labdhvā tapasogreṇa brāhmaṇatvaṃ mahāyaśāḥ vicacāra mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ kṛtakāmaḥ suropamaḥ
english: Having won brahminhood by fierce austerity, that man of great renown, his desire fulfilled and god-like in his splendour, roamed across the whole earth.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tīrthavare rāmaḥ pradāya vividhaṃ vasu payasvinīs tathā dhenūr yānāni śayanāni ca
english: At that excellent sacred ford Rāma bestowed wealth of many kinds — milk-giving cows, draught animals, and couches —

sanskrit: tathā vastrāṇy alaṃkāraṃ bhakṣyaṃ peyaṃ ca śobhanam adadān mudito rājan pūjayitvā dvijottamān
english: and garments too, and ornaments, and fine food and drink. Gladly, O king, he gave these gifts, having honoured the foremost of the twice-born.

sanskrit: yayau rājaṃs tato rāmo bakasyāśramam antikāt yatra tepe tapas tīvraṃ dālbhyo baka iti śrutiḥ
english: Then, O king, Rāma went on from there to the hermitage of Baka close by, where, as tradition tells, Baka the son of Dalbha had performed fierce austerity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca brahmayonibhir ākīrṇaṃ jagāma yadunandanaḥ yatra dālbhyo bako rājan paśvarthaṃ sumahātapāḥ juhāva dhṛtarāṣṭrasya rāṣṭraṃ vaicitravīryiṇaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The delight of the Yadus went to that place thronged with men of brahmin lineage, where, O king, Baka the son of Dalbha, of mighty austerity, for the sake of cattle once offered up into the fire the kingdom of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Vicitravīrya.

sanskrit: tapasā ghorarūpeṇa karśayan deham ātmanaḥ krodhena mahatāviṣṭo dharmātmā vai pratāpavān
english: Wasting his own body with austerity of dreadful aspect, that righteous and mighty sage was seized by a great anger.

sanskrit: purā hi naimiṣeyāṇāṃ satre dvādaśavārṣike vṛtte viśvajito 'nte vai pāñcālān ṛṣayo 'gaman
english: For long ago, when the twelve-year sacrificial session of the seers of Naimiṣa had been completed, at the close of the Viśvajit rite the sages went to the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: tatreśvaram ayācanta dakṣiṇārthaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ balānvitān vatsatarān nirvyādhīn ekaviṃśatim
english: There those wise men asked the lord of that land for a sacrificial fee: twenty-one strong young calves, free of disease.

sanskrit: tān abravīd bako vṛddho vibhajadhvaṃ paśūn iti paśūn etān ahaṃ tyaktvā bhikṣiṣye rājasattamam
english: To them aged Baka said: 'Divide these cattle among yourselves; for my part, leaving these beasts aside, I shall beg of the best of kings.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rājann ṛṣīn sarvān pratāpavān jagāma dhṛtarāṣṭrasya bhavanaṃ brāhmaṇottamaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to all the seers, O king, that mighty and foremost of brahmins went to the dwelling of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: sa samīpagato bhūtvā dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janeśvaram ayācata paśūn dālbhyaḥ sa cainaṃ ruṣito 'bravīt
english: Drawing near to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, the son of Dalbha begged him for cattle; but that king answered him in anger:

sanskrit: yadṛcchayā mṛtā dṛṣṭvā gās tadā nṛpasattama etān paśūn naya kṣipraṃ brahmabandho yadīcchasi
english: 'Look on these cows that have died of their own accord, O best of kings' — so the king said — 'take these beasts at once, you wretched excuse for a brahmin, if you wish.'

sanskrit: ṛṣis tv atha vacaḥ śrutvā cintayām āsa dharmavit aho bata nṛśaṃsaṃ vai vākyam ukto 'smi saṃsadi
english: The seer, knower of dharma, hearing these words, fell to thinking: 'Alas, cruel indeed is the speech with which I have been addressed in the assembly!'

sanskrit: cintayitvā muhūrtaṃ ca roṣāviṣṭo dvijottamaḥ matiṃ cakre vināśāya dhṛtarāṣṭrasya bhūpateḥ
english: Having pondered a while, that foremost of the twice-born, seized by wrath, set his mind upon the destruction of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: sa utkṛtya mṛtānāṃ vai māṃsāni dvijasattamaḥ juhāva dhṛtarāṣṭrasya rāṣṭraṃ narapateḥ purā
english: That best of the twice-born, cutting the flesh from the dead cattle, then offered up into the fire the kingdom of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: avakīrṇe sarasvatyās tīrthe prajvālya pāvakam bako dālbhyo mahārāja niyamaṃ param āsthitaḥ sa tair eva juhāvāsya rāṣṭraṃ māṃsair mahātapāḥ
english: At a secluded ford of the Sarasvatī, having kindled the sacred fire, Baka the son of Dalbha, O great king, took up a most rigorous vow; and that sage of mighty austerity offered up his kingdom with those very pieces of flesh.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu vidhivat satre saṃpravṛtte sudāruṇe akṣīyata tato rāṣṭraṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya pārthiva
english: When that most terrible sacrificial session had been duly begun, the kingdom of Dhṛtarāṣṭra began to waste away, O king.

sanskrit: chidyamānaṃ yathānantaṃ vanaṃ paraśunā vibho babhūvāpahataṃ tac cāpy avakīrṇam acetanam
english: Like a boundless forest hewn down by the axe, O lord, that kingdom became ruined, scattered, and bereft of sense.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tad avakīrṇaṃ tu rāṣṭraṃ sa manujādhipaḥ babhūva durmanā rājaṃś cintayām āsa ca prabhuḥ
english: Seeing his kingdom so laid waste, that lord of men grew downcast, O king, and the sovereign fell to brooding.

sanskrit: mokṣārtham akarod yatnaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ sahitaḥ purā athāsau pārthivaḥ khinnas te ca viprās tadā nṛpa
english: He strove together with his brahmins to win release from it; yet that king remained distressed, O king, and so too were those learned men.

sanskrit: yadā cāpi na śaknoti rāṣṭraṃ mocayituṃ nṛpa atha vaiprāśnikāṃs tatra papraccha janamejaya
english: And when he could not free his kingdom, O king, he then questioned the readers of omens there, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: tato vaiprāśnikāḥ prāhuḥ paśuviprakṛtas tvayā māṃsair abhijuhotīti tava rāṣṭraṃ munir bakaḥ
english: Then the readers of omens declared: 'The sage Baka, slighted by you in the matter of cattle, is offering up your kingdom with flesh as oblation.'

sanskrit: tena te hūyamānasya rāṣṭrasyāsya kṣayo mahān tasyaitat tapasaḥ karma yena te hy anayo mahān apāṃ kuñje sarasvatyās taṃ prasādaya pārthiva
english: 'By his oblation this great ruin has come upon your kingdom; this is the working of his austerity, by which this great calamity has fallen upon you. In a watery thicket of the Sarasvatī, O king, win his favour.'

sanskrit: sarasvatīṃ tato gatvā sa rājā bakam abravīt nipatya śirasā bhūmau prāñjalir bharatarṣabha
english: Then the king went to the Sarasvatī and, prostrating with his head to the ground, his palms joined, said to Baka, O bull of the Bharatas:

sanskrit: prasādaye tvā bhagavann aparādhaṃ kṣamasva me mama dīnasya lubdhasya maurkhyeṇa hatacetasaḥ tvaṃ gatis tvaṃ ca me nāthaḥ prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: 'I beseech your favour, O holy one; forgive my offence — wretched, greedy, and bereft of sense through my own folly that I am. You are my refuge, you are my protector; deign to show me grace.'

sanskrit: taṃ tathā vilapantaṃ tu śokopahatacetasam dṛṣṭvā tasya kṛpā jajñe rāṣṭraṃ tac ca vyamocayat
english: Seeing him lamenting thus, his mind overwhelmed with grief, the sage was moved to pity, and he set that kingdom free.

sanskrit: ṛṣiḥ prasannas tasyābhūt saṃrambhaṃ ca vihāya saḥ mokṣārthaṃ tasya rāṣṭrasya juhāva punar āhutim
english: The seer became gracious toward him and, laying aside his fury, offered up another oblation for the release of that kingdom.

sanskrit: mokṣayitvā tato rāṣṭraṃ pratigṛhya paśūn bahūn hṛṣṭātmā naimiṣāraṇyaṃ jagāma punar eva hi
english: Having freed the kingdom and received many head of cattle, with a glad heart he went back once more to the Naimiṣa forest.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭro 'pi dharmātmā svasthacetā mahāmanāḥ svam eva nagaraṃ rājā pratipede maharddhimat
english: And the righteous, high-minded king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, now easy in mind, returned to his own most prosperous city.

sanskrit: tatra tīrthe mahārāja bṛhaspatir udāradhīḥ asurāṇām abhāvāya bhāvāya ca divaukasām
english: At that ford, O great king, Bṛhaspati of noble intellect — for the undoing of the Asuras and the flourishing of the dwellers in heaven —

sanskrit: māṃsair api juhāveṣṭim akṣīyanta tato 'surāḥ daivatair api saṃbhagnā jitakāśibhir āhave
english: performed a sacrifice with offerings of flesh as well; and thereupon the Asuras began to waste away, shattered too in battle by the gods, who shone with the look of victors.

sanskrit: tatrāpi vidhivad dattvā brāhmaṇebhyo mahāyaśāḥ vājinaḥ kuñjarāṃś caiva rathāṃś cāśvatarīyutān
english: There too that man of great renown duly gave to the brahmins horses and elephants and chariots yoked with mules,

sanskrit: ratnāni ca mahārhāṇi dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ ca puṣkalam yayau tīrthaṃ mahābāhur yāyātaṃ pṛthivīpate
english: and gems of great worth, and wealth and abundant grain; then that mighty-armed one went to the ford of Yayāti, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: yatra yajñe yayātes tu mahārāja sarasvatī sarpiḥ payaś ca susrāva nāhuṣasya mahātmanaḥ
english: There, O great king, at the sacrifice of Yayāti, the great-souled son of Nahuṣa, the Sarasvatī flowed forth with ghee and milk.

sanskrit: tatreṣṭvā puruṣavyāghro yayātiḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ ākrāmad ūrdhvaṃ mudito lebhe lokāṃś ca puṣkalān
english: Having there performed sacrifice, Yayāti, tiger among men and lord of the earth, ascended on high rejoicing, and won abundant worlds.

sanskrit: yayāter yajamānasya yatra rājan sarasvatī prasṛtā pradadau kāmān brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām
english: Where, O king, for Yayāti as he sacrificed, the Sarasvatī streamed forth and granted the desires of the great-souled brahmins —

sanskrit: yatra yatra hi yo vipro yān yān kāmān abhīpsati tatra tatra saricchreṣṭhā sasarja subahūn rasān
english: for wherever any brahmin wished for whatever he desired, there and there that best of rivers poured forth manifold flavours.

sanskrit: tatra devāḥ sagandharvāḥ prītā yajñasya saṃpadā vismitā mānuṣāś cāsan dṛṣṭvā tāṃ yajñasaṃpadam
english: There the gods along with the Gandharvas were delighted at the splendour of the sacrifice, and the mortals too were amazed to behold that perfection of the rite.

sanskrit: tatas tālaketur mahādharmasetur; mahātmā kṛtātmā mahādānanityaḥ vasiṣṭhāpavāhaṃ mahābhīmavegaṃ; dhṛtātmā jitātmā samabhyājagāma
english: Then he of the palm-tree banner, a great bulwark of dharma, high-souled and perfected in spirit, ever devoted to lavish giving, steadfast and self-mastered, came to the place of Vasiṣṭha's carrying-off, where the river had run with mighty and terrible force.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca vasiṣṭhasyāpavāho vai bhīmavegaḥ kathaṃ nu saḥ kimarthaṃ ca saricchreṣṭhā tam ṛṣiṃ pratyavāhayat
english: Janamejaya said: How came that carrying-off of Vasiṣṭha, of fearful swiftness, to be? And why did that best of rivers bear the seer away?

sanskrit: kena cāsyābhavad vairaṃ kāraṇaṃ kiṃ ca tat prabho śaṃsa pṛṣṭo mahāprājña na hi tṛpyāmi kathyatām
english: And with whom did he have this enmity, and what was its cause, O lord? Being asked, O most wise one, tell it; for I am not sated — let it be told.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca viśvāmitrasya caivarṣer vasiṣṭhasya ca bhārata bhṛśaṃ vairam abhūd rājaṃs tapaḥspardhākṛtaṃ mahat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Between the seer Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha, O Bhārata, there arose a fierce and mighty enmity, O king, born of their rivalry in austerity.

sanskrit: āśramo vai vasiṣṭhasya sthāṇutīrthe 'bhavan mahān pūrvataḥ paścimaś cāsīd viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ
english: The great hermitage of Vasiṣṭha stood at the ford of Sthāṇu on the eastern side, while that of the wise Viśvāmitra lay to the west.

sanskrit: yatra sthāṇur mahārāja taptavān sumahat tapaḥ yatrāsya karma tad ghoraṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: There, O great king, Sthāṇu performed exceedingly great austerity, and there, as the wise relate, he wrought that dreadful deed.

sanskrit: yatreṣṭvā bhagavān sthāṇuḥ pūjayitvā sarasvatīm sthāpayām āsa tat tīrthaṃ sthāṇutīrtham iti prabho
english: Where the lord Sthāṇu, having sacrificed and worshipped the Sarasvatī, established that ford, which is therefore called Sthāṇutīrtha, O lord.

sanskrit: tatra sarve surāḥ skandam abhyaṣiñcan narādhipa senāpatyena mahatā surārivinibarhaṇam
english: There, O ruler of men, all the gods consecrated Skanda, slayer of the foes of the gods, with the great office of commander of their host.

sanskrit: tasmin sarasvatītīrthe viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ vasiṣṭhaṃ cālayām āsa tapasogreṇa tac chṛṇu
english: At that ford of the Sarasvatī, the great sage Viśvāmitra unsettled Vasiṣṭha by fierce austerity — hear how it was.

sanskrit: viśvāmitravasiṣṭhau tāv ahany ahani bhārata spardhāṃ tapaḥkṛtāṃ tīvrāṃ cakratus tau tapodhanau
english: Day after day, O Bhārata, those two — Viśvāmitra and Vasiṣṭha, both rich in austerity — carried on their fierce contest born of penance.

sanskrit: tatrāpy adhikasaṃtāpo viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ dṛṣṭvā tejo vasiṣṭhasya cintām abhijagāma ha tasya buddhir iyaṃ hy āsīd dharmanityasya bhārata
english: There the great sage Viśvāmitra, burning all the more, seeing the splendour of Vasiṣṭha, fell into deep thought; and this was the resolve that came to that ever-righteous one, O Bhārata:

sanskrit: iyaṃ sarasvatī tūrṇaṃ matsamīpaṃ tapodhanam ānayiṣyati vegena vasiṣṭhaṃ japatāṃ varam ihāgataṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ haniṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ
english: 'This Sarasvatī shall swiftly bring near to me, by the force of her current, Vasiṣṭha rich in austerity, that best of those who chant the sacred words; and when that foremost of the twice-born is brought hither, I shall slay him — of this there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: evaṃ niścitya bhagavān viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ sasmāra saritāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ
english: Having so resolved, the lord Viśvāmitra, that great sage, his eyes red with anger, called to mind the best of rivers.

sanskrit: sā dhyātā muninā tena vyākulatvaṃ jagāma ha jajñe cainaṃ mahāvīryaṃ mahākopaṃ ca bhāminī
english: Summoned by the sage's thought, she fell into agitation, for the fair one knew him to be of great might and great wrath.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ vepamānā vivarṇā prāñjalis tadā upatasthe munivaraṃ viśvāmitraṃ sarasvatī
english: Then, trembling and pale, her palms joined, the Sarasvatī came and stood before that best of sages, Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: hatavīrā yathā nārī sābhavad duḥkhitā bhṛśam brūhi kiṃ karavāṇīti provāca munisattamam
english: Like a woman whose husband has been slain, she was sorely grieved, and she said to that best of sages: 'Tell me — what shall I do?'

sanskrit: tām uvāca muniḥ kruddho vasiṣṭhaṃ śīghram ānaya yāvad enaṃ nihanmy adya tac chrutvā vyathitā nadī
english: The angry sage said to her: 'Bring Vasiṣṭha quickly, that I may slay him this very day.' Hearing this, the river was stricken with dread.

sanskrit: sāñjaliṃ tu tataḥ kṛtvā puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇā vivyathe suvirūḍheva latā vāyusamīritā
english: Then she, whose eyes were like lotus-petals, joining her palms, trembled like a well-grown creeper shaken by the wind.

sanskrit: tathāgatāṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vepamānāṃ kṛtāñjalim viśvāmitro 'bravīt kruddho vasiṣṭhaṃ śīghram ānaya
english: Seeing her come thus, trembling, with palms joined, Viśvāmitra in anger said: 'Bring Vasiṣṭha quickly!'

sanskrit: tato bhītā saricchreṣṭhā cintayām āsa bhārata ubhayoḥ śāpayor bhītā katham etad bhaviṣyati
english: Then that best of rivers, afraid, fell to thinking, O Bhārata, dreading the curse of both: 'How shall this come about?'

sanskrit: sābhigamya vasiṣṭhaṃ tu imam artham acodayat yad uktā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā
english: And going to Vasiṣṭha, she set forth this matter — all that the best of rivers had been told by the wise Viśvāmitra —

sanskrit: ubhayoḥ śāpayor bhītā vepamānā punaḥ punaḥ cintayitvā mahāśāpam ṛṣivitrāsitā bhṛśam
english: trembling again and again in fear of the curse of both, brooding upon the dread curse, sorely terrified by the seers.

sanskrit: tāṃ kṛśāṃ ca vivarṇāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā cintāsamanvitām uvāca rājan dharmātmā vasiṣṭho dvipadāṃ varaḥ
english: Seeing her wasted and pale and filled with anxiety, the righteous Vasiṣṭha, best of men, O king, said to her:

sanskrit: trāhy ātmānaṃ saricchreṣṭhe vaha māṃ śīghragāminī viśvāmitraḥ śaped dhi tvāṃ mā kṛthās tvaṃ vicāraṇām
english: 'Save yourself, O best of rivers; swift-flowing one, carry me away — for else Viśvāmitra will curse you. Do not hesitate.'

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kṛpāśīlasya sā sarit cintayām āsa kauravya kiṃ kṛtaṃ sukṛtaṃ bhavet
english: Hearing that word of the compassionate sage, the river pondered, O Kaurava: 'What course, if taken, would be well done?'

sanskrit: tasyāś cintā samutpannā vasiṣṭho mayy atīva hi kṛtavān hi dayāṃ nityaṃ tasya kāryaṃ hitaṃ mayā
english: This thought arose in her: 'Vasiṣṭha has ever shown me great kindness; surely his good must be wrought by me.'

sanskrit: atha kūle svake rājañ japantam ṛṣisattamam juhvānaṃ kauśikaṃ prekṣya sarasvaty abhyacintayat
english: Then, O king, beholding upon her own bank the son of Kuśika, that best of seers, as he chanted and offered oblation, the Sarasvatī reflected:

sanskrit: idam antaram ity eva tataḥ sā saritāṃ varā kūlāpahāram akarot svena vegena sā sarit
english: 'This is the moment.' And so that best of rivers tore away her own bank with the force of her current.

sanskrit: tena kūlāpahāreṇa maitrāvaruṇir auhyata uhyamānaś ca tuṣṭāva tadā rājan sarasvatīm
english: By that carrying-away of the bank the son of Mitra and Varuṇa was borne off; and as he was borne along, O king, he then praised the Sarasvatī:

sanskrit: pitāmahasya sarasaḥ pravṛttāsi sarasvati vyāptaṃ cedaṃ jagat sarvaṃ tavaivāmbhobhir uttamaiḥ
english: 'From the lake of the Grandsire have you sprung forth, O Sarasvatī, and all this world is pervaded by your most excellent waters.'

sanskrit: tvam evākāśagā devi megheṣūtsṛjase payaḥ sarvāś cāpas tvam eveti tvatto vayam adhīmahe
english: 'You, O goddess, moving through the sky, release your waters in the clouds; you alone are all the waters, and from you do we draw our sustenance.'

sanskrit: puṣṭir dyutis tathā kīrtiḥ siddhir vṛddhir umā tathā tvam eva vāṇī svāhā tvaṃ tvayy āyattam idaṃ jagat tvam eva sarvabhūteṣu vasasīha caturvidhā
english: 'You are nourishment, radiance, and renown, attainment, increase, and Umā; you alone are Speech, you are Svāhā; upon you this world depends, and you dwell here in all beings in your fourfold form.'

sanskrit: evaṃ sarasvatī rājan stūyamānā maharṣiṇā vegenovāha taṃ vipraṃ viśvāmitrāśramaṃ prati nyavedayata cābhīkṣṇaṃ viśvāmitrāya taṃ munim
english: Thus praised by the great seer, O king, the Sarasvatī bore that brahmin swiftly toward the hermitage of Viśvāmitra, and again and again she presented the sage to Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: tam ānītaṃ sarasvatyā dṛṣṭvā kopasamanvitaḥ athānveṣat praharaṇaṃ vasiṣṭhāntakaraṃ tadā
english: Seeing him brought by the Sarasvatī, filled with rage, Viśvāmitra then sought out a weapon to make an end of Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: taṃ tu kruddham abhiprekṣya brahmahatyābhayān nadī apovāha vasiṣṭhaṃ tu prācīṃ diśam atandritā ubhayoḥ kurvatī vākyaṃ vañcayitvā tu gādhijam
english: But seeing him enraged, the river, from fear of the slaying of a brahmin, carried Vasiṣṭha off untiringly toward the eastern quarter — thus obeying the word of both, yet outwitting the son of Gādhi.

sanskrit: tato 'pavāhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā vasiṣṭham ṛṣisattamam abravīd atha saṃkruddho viśvāmitro hy amarṣaṇaḥ
english: Then, seeing Vasiṣṭha, that best of seers, borne away, the wrathful and unforgiving Viśvāmitra said:

sanskrit: yasmān mā tvaṃ saricchreṣṭhe vañcayitvā punar gatā śoṇitaṃ vaha kalyāṇi rakṣogrāmaṇisaṃmatam
english: 'Since you, O best of rivers, having deceived me, have slipped away again — flow with blood, fair one, the kind that demon-chiefs delight in!'

sanskrit: tataḥ sarasvatī śaptā viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā avahac choṇitonmiśraṃ toyaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ tadā
english: Then the Sarasvatī, cursed by the wise Viśvāmitra, carried water mingled with blood for a whole year thereafter.

sanskrit: atharṣayaś ca devāś ca gandharvāpsarasas tathā sarasvatīṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā babhūvur bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ
english: And the seers and the gods, the Gandharvas and the Apsarases, seeing the Sarasvatī in such a state, were sorely grieved.

sanskrit: evaṃ vasiṣṭhāpavāho loke khyāto janādhipa āgacchac ca punar mārgaṃ svam eva saritāṃ varā
english: Thus came the carrying-off of Vasiṣṭha to be famed in the world, O ruler of men; and that best of rivers came again to her own course.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā śaptā tena kruddhena viśvāmitreṇa dhīmatā tasmiṃs tīrthavare śubhre śoṇitaṃ samupāvahat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: She, cursed by the wrathful and wise Viśvāmitra, carried blood at that bright and excellent ford.

sanskrit: athājagmus tato rājan rākṣasās tatra bhārata tatra te śoṇitaṃ sarve pibantaḥ sukham āsate
english: Then, O king, the Rākṣasas came thither, O Bhārata, and there they all dwelt at ease, drinking the blood.
